title: Ministère de l'Intérieur France-Visas Long-Stay Visa and Passeport Talent Framework
source: Direction Générale des Étrangers en France, Ministère de l'Intérieur
content:
Non-European Union citizens relocating to France for work, business, or studies must obtain a Long-Stay Visa equivalent to a residence permit (VLS-TS) or a multi-year 'Passeport Talent' residence permit.

The Passeport Talent is designed for highly qualified employees, startup founders, researchers, and executives, granting residency for up to four years with simplified family reunification rights. VLS-TS holders must validate their visa online within three months of arrival via the Étrangers en France portal (ANEF) and pay the mandatory residence permit tax (taxe de séjour).

Residence permits must be renewed at the departmental Préfecture before expiry. After five years of uninterrupted lawful residence, foreign nationals can apply for a 10-year European long-term resident card or French naturalisation.

title: Assurance Maladie (Ameli) French Social Security and Carte Vitale Health Coverage
source: Caisse Nationale de l'Assurance Maladie (CNAM / Ameli)
publisher: Ministère de la Santé et de la Prévention, France
content:
France operates the Protection Universelle Maladie (PUMA), guaranteeing access to state healthcare coverage for all individuals working or residing in France on a stable and regular basis (at least three months).

Foreign residents register with their local Caisse Primaire d'Assurance Maladie (CPAM) to obtain a provisional and then permanent Social Security Number (numéro de sécurité sociale) and a green electronic healthcare smartcard known as the Carte Vitale.

The state health insurance reimburses approximately 70% of standard doctor consultations and hospital treatments. The remaining balance (ticket modérateur) is typically covered by complementary private health insurance (Mutuelle), which employers are legally obligated to provide and subsidize for employees.

title: Ville de Paris Municipal Administration and Resident Services
content:
The City of Paris is divided into 20 municipal arrondissements, each served by a local Town Hall (Mairie d'Arrondissement) administering civil registry, school enrollments, and municipal waste services.

Residential leases (baux d'habitation) in Paris are subject to rent control (encadrement des loyers), establishing maximum reference rent caps per square meter depending on neighborhood and construction era. Security deposits are legally limited to one month's rent for unfurnished apartments and two months' rent for furnished rentals.

Paris provides municipal services, crèches, public libraries, and the Paris Welcome Desk assisting foreign students and researchers with administrative formalities upon arrival.

title: Île-de-France Mobilités / RATP Public Transit Network and Navigo Pass System
source: Régie Autonome des Transports Parisiens (RATP) / Île-de-France Mobilités
content:
Public transit across Paris and the Île-de-France region is coordinated by Île-de-France Mobilités and operated primarily by RATP and SNCF, encompassing 16 Paris Métro lines, 5 RER express train lines, 13 tramway routes, and hundreds of bus lines.

The primary fare card is the Navigo pass, available as a physical smartcard or on compatible smartphones via NFC. Subscriptions are available weekly, monthly, or annually. French labour law mandates that employers in Paris reimburse at least 50% of the cost of employees' public transit passes.

Single journeys can be paid via dematerialized t+ tickets on smartcards or smartphones. Metro trains operate daily from 05:30 until approximately 01:15 on weekdays and 02:15 on Fridays and Saturdays.
